lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Guided practice: requests, declines, and boundaries

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic requests, declines, and boundaries task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner works from two short scenario prompts on this task sheet, one where they need to ask a coach or teacher for something specific, and one where a friend has asked them for something they need to turn down, and drafts both messages using the three-part template, without sending either message to anyone.
safetyNotes: Both messages drafted in this lesson are practice only; neither is sent to a real recipient, and no real contact information is needed to complete this task sheet.

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l03-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l03-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l03-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l03-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Which message was harder to keep clear and boundaried without over-apologizing, and what specific sentence did you have to revise to fix that?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l03-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l03-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g9-u05-l03-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Request clarity: Request states the situation, the specific ask, and one follow-up question, each in its own clear sentence. | Boundary clarity in the decline: Decline states a clear refusal in one sentence without blaming a rule or third party. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l03-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner draft a third message declining a request from an adult outside their household, such as a coach asking them to take on an extra commitment, using the same three-part template and noting what changes when the recipient is an adult rather than a friend.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic requests, declines, and boundaries task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: paper or a document
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: requests, declines, and boundaries worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner works from two short scenario prompts on this task sheet, one where they need to ask a coach or teacher for something specific, and one where a friend has asked them for something they need to turn down, and drafts both messages using the three-part template, without sending either message to anyone.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact requests, declines, and boundaries decision or action.
Model move 2: Read the two scenarios below.

Model move 3: Draft your request message for Scenario 1 using the three-part template: state the situation in one sentence, state exactly what you're asking for, then ask one specific follow-up question (such as a possible time).

Model check: Request clarity: Request states the situation, the specific ask, and one follow-up question, each in its own clear sentence. | Boundary clarity in the decline: Decline states a clear refusal in one sentence without blaming a rule or third party.

resources.title: requests, declines, and boundaries action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for requests, declines, and boundaries.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: requests, declines, and boundaries coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner works from two short scenario prompts on this task sheet, one where they need to ask a coach or teacher for something specific, and one where a friend has asked them for something they need to turn down, and drafts both messages using the three-part template, without sending either message to anyone.
Coach direction: Read the two scenarios below.
Learner prompt: For each scenario, write down what makes it uncomfortable to bring up, and what you actually want the outcome to be.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: requests, declines, and boundaries complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Draft your request message for Scenario 1 using the three-part template: state the situation in one sentence, state exactly what you're asking for, then ask one specific follow-up question (such as a possible time).
Response 1 (t2-p1): My message states the situation in one sentence without over-explaining or apologizing more than once.
Response 2 (t2-p2): My message states exactly what I'm asking for in a single clear sentence.
Response 3 (t2-p3): My message ends with one specific follow-up question, such as offering a time or asking what would work.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: requests, declines, and boundaries minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Which message was harder to keep clear and boundaried without over-apologizing, and what specific sentence did you have to revise to fix that?

Success checks: Request clarity: Request states the situation, the specific ask, and one follow-up question, each in its own clear sentence. | Boundary clarity in the decline: Decline states a clear refusal in one sentence without blaming a rule or third party.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: requests, declines, and boundaries supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l03-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g9-u05-l03-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional requests, declines, and boundaries condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Request clarity: Request states the situation, the specific ask, and one follow-up question, each in its own clear sentence. | Boundary clarity in the decline: Decline states a clear refusal in one sentence without blaming a rule or third party..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l03-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guidedFirstAttempt.setup: The learner works from two short scenario prompts on this task sheet, one where they need to ask a coach or teacher for something specific, and one where a friend has asked them for something they need to turn down, and drafts both messages using the three-part template, without sending either message to anyone.
guidedFirstAttempt.prompt: For each scenario, write down what makes it uncomfortable to bring up, and what you actually want the outcome to be.
coachMoves: Ask the learner to name the condition.
Point to one model step only.
Give feedback against one observable success check.
guidedFirstAttempt.successCondition: Request clarity: Request states the situation, the specific ask, and one follow-up question, each in its own clear sentence.
guidedFirstAttempt.correctionTurn: Use the fresh condition on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l03-guided-card: change one constraint, redo only the affected move, and state why the corrected move now meets the success check.

simulationRoute.title: requests, declines, and boundaries — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: Complete the requests, declines, and boundaries task using the fictional condition and invented, non-sensitive details on the delivered independent card.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

learnerEvidence: one revision when a step changed
evidence.reflectionPrompt: Which message was harder to keep clear and boundaried without over-apologizing, and what specific sentence did you have to revise to fix that?
observableCriteria: Request clarity: Request states the situation, the specific ask, and one follow-up question, each in its own clear sentence.
Boundary clarity in the decline: Decline states a clear refusal in one sentence without blaming a rule or third party.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l03-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l03-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g9-u05-l03-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Request clarity: Request states the situation, the specific ask, and one follow-up question, each in its own clear sentence. | Boundary clarity in the decline: Decline states a clear refusal in one sentence without blaming a rule or third party.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g9-u05-l03-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
